quotes.text: Notifications don't have to be treated like paper slips shoved under a digital door. They can ask for action directly. They can carry buttons, fields, and contexts so users can respond instantly.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the core idea of actionable notifications.

quotes.text: Lists aren't passive storage. They are the schema, the definition of what your workflow actually means. Every column sets a rule, every field enforces structure.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes Microsoft Lists as the data schema behind every card.

quotes.text: Use the right trigger so the card lands at the right moment, not every possible moment.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A compact rule against notification spam from Power Automate flows.

quotes.text: Confirm your team's connector is authenticated as an account with rights to post in the target channel or chat. Otherwise, the flow reports success, but nothing arrives.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical troubleshooting tip for a common silent failure.

quotes.text: Show your card to someone who hasn't seen it before. If they can't tell what to do in under three seconds, simplify it, cut words, reduce buttons
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A simple, repeatable usability test for card design.

chapters.title: Why your Teams notifications are dumb
Power Automate: wiring it all together

takeaways: Static Teams notifications get ignored because they carry no action, while Adaptive Cards bring approve, snooze or update buttons straight into the chat.
Clean, typed columns in Microsoft Lists are the schema that makes cards clear, and card fields should map directly to list column names.
Wire cards with Power Automate using targeted triggers, a verified Teams connector and a pilot group, and keep each card to one or two actions.
hook: Most Teams notifications are static FYI pings that nobody acts on. This episode shows Microsoft 365 admins and makers how to combine Microsoft Lists, Adaptive Cards and Power Automate into actionable notifications that users can approve or snooze without leaving chat.
